candidate_scores.exact_behavior: For g_k<k+1, some orbits are skipped; for g_k=k+1, the frozen age map is a bijection; for g_k>k+1, later events emit OVERFLOW.
For g_k<k+1, orbits are skipped; for g_k=k+1, it is a bijection; for g_k>k+1, at least one orbit repeats.
Consecutive residues give a permutation of O2(k) only when the interval has exactly k+1 events; shorter gaps skip and longer gaps repeat. The primary index does not prove the interval length.
Its image uses at most two orbit labels; for k>=2, |O2(k)|=k+1>=3 so surjectivity is impossible. The realized bit is also post-realization data, not a predictor of the next jump.

cardinality_lemma.proof: Conditions 1-3 make a bijection between the g_k primary event IDs and the k+1 quotient-frontier orbits.
cardinality_lemma.statement: If every event in a finite k-layer occupancy interval maps to one orbit in O2(k), with no skipped orbit and no repeated orbit, then the map is a bijection and g_k=|O2(k)|=k+1.

frozen_gap_freedom_conflict.consequence: No bijective primary-gap -> O2(k) correspondence is forced by the frozen Stage-X/Y/Z semantics.
frozen_gap_freedom_conflict.same_prefix_witness: For any k>=1, keep all prior gaps fixed and choose two continuations with g_k=k and g_k=k+2. Both are allowed; neither equals k+1.
frozen_gap_freedom_conflict.statement: Stage Z freezes that every positive integer g can occur as g_k=A_(k+1)-A_k in a globally extendable binary staircase, with the earlier activation history held fixed.
